demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: Your lane: the note goes in, and the switches
demos.purpose: make ingest-one puts one object under acme's prefix in the uploads bucket and waits for the worker's ingest_ok line. The note has no entry in acme's registry, so it ingests as doc_type unknown, as the next step's code says. make sources lists the ledger's current versions; the grep keeps the note's row. Then export the two agent addresses the rest of the page uses, and read the peer's switches: /health says tool_pins off and agent_fence false as lesson 10.6's deploy script leaves them. There is no make target for the switches: they are service environment variables, set the way make limits-drill sets others. The update makes a new documind-chat revision that serves at once, as long as the service's traffic follows its latest revision, which make limits-drill and make handoff check the same way before they change a variable; gcloud run services update-traffic documind-chat --to-latest puts it back if it does not. Step 9 turns them off again around the same cell, and step 12 leaves them off.

demos.purpose: Listing the kit's server in process imports it, so the venv takes the server's requirements (fastmcp 3.4.7 and the mcp client) and the peer's (google-adk 2.8.0), which pin the same side of the mcp 1.x line. make pin-tools rewrites tool_pins.json byte for byte when nothing changed; CHECK=1 says so and exits 0. The last line puts the kit back.

demos.heading: Poisoned tools, on your machine: the pins
demos.purpose: Optional, the author's shell: the kit's peer on your machine against the poisoned server, in three tabs, with TOOL_PINS off and then on. The pin checks before it prove the same refusal without a model call.

steps.heading: Poisoned tools, on your machine: the pins
steps.subheading: Do it: the peer against the poisoned server
steps.purpose: The kit's own peer, on your machine, pointed at the fixture with MCP_AUTH=none, so no token is minted and no account impersonated; SELF_URL empty, so its card says localhost. Gemini answers, through your own credentials, so each task costs a few model calls. Ask one inventory question three times: pins off against the default shape, pins on against the same, and pins on against RUG=1. With the pins off, summarise_inbox and its sentence are in the model's hands; with them on, the peer's log says tool_unpinned and the model never sees that tool; against the rug pull, the honest retrieve is the one dropped, because its fingerprint moved.
steps.label: bash — the author's shell (the kit's peer on your machine against the poisoned server: Gemini answers, so a few rupees)
steps.expected: [awaiting the author's run: data/pins_peer.txt]

A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The pin back is a separate window on purpose: pasted together with the line above, it would put acme straight back on RAG Engine before the lesson began. Leave it until the lesson's last step is done.
